name: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting
executive_summary: Prompt the model with worked examples that show step-by-step reasoning, so it reasons in steps before answering instead of jumping straight to a conclusion.
description: Few-shot exemplars that include intermediate reasoning steps, not just final answers, are shown before the target question. The model learns from the pattern to produce its own intermediate steps, which substantially improves performance on multi-step arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks. It is the foundation nearly every later reasoning-elicitation technique builds on or varies.
when_to_use: The task requires more than one logical or arithmetic step to reach a correct answer.
You have or can write 2-8 worked examples in the target domain.
when_not_to_use: The task is a single lookup or classification with no multi-step structure — CoT adds tokens without adding accuracy.
Model is small enough that CoT exemplars don't reliably improve over direct answering (an empirically observed emergent-capability threshold).
known_pitfalls: A plausible-looking chain does not guarantee a correct answer; the model can rationalize a wrong answer just as fluently as a right one.
Long chains increase token cost roughly linearly without a matching accuracy gain past a task-dependent point.

primary_source.authors: Wei, Wang, Schuurmans, Bosma, Ichter, Xia, Chi, Le, Zhou
primary_source.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

variables.description: The worked step-by-step reasoning for example 1

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
